title: Diabetes incidence register in young age
summary:
Diabetes mellitus is a group of metabolic diseases that cause persistently high blood sugar levels.  In the general population, type 2 diabetes is the most common form of diabetes. Among children and adolescens, however, type 1 diabetes occurs most frequently. 

DIREGT is a well-established epidemiological register that has been in operation for three decades. In 1992, the motivation for establishing the register of newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes was to provide the most reliable possible estimate of the number of newly diagnosed cases of type 1  diabetes and the total number of children and adolescents living with type 1 diabetes.
Prior to this initiative, there were insufficient data on new diagnoses of type 1 diabetes in Germany. The inclusion criteria and data sources have been continuously expanded to achieve the most comprehensive possible coverage of new diagnoses of type 1 and type 2 diabetes in North Rhine-Westphalia (< 35 years) and type 1 diabetes in Germany (< 5 years).
The goal of DIREGT is the structured collection and scientific analysis of data on new diagnoses of type 1 and type 2 diabetes to describe the prevalence, trends over time, and risks of type 1 diabetes in children under five years of age in Germany and of type 1 and type 2 diabetes in individuals under 35 years of age in North Rhine-Westphalia.
The anonymous collection of data on new diabetes diagnoses from physicians is limited exclusively to the initial diagnosis of diabetes in childhood, adolescence, and young adulthood.
The registry collects data from three sources:
The German Paediatric Surveillance Unit (GPSU) is an active surveillance system that includes nearly all pediatric hospitals in Germany and has been used since the establishment of the register.
In addition, the German Diabetes Center (DDZ) receives reports from internal medicine, pediatric, and general practice clinics, as well as from diabetes-specialized practices and the diabetes and internal medicine departments of hospitals in North Rhine-Westphalia.
Since 1998, the DDZ has also been collaborating with the Institute of Epidemiology and Medical Biometry at the University of Ulm, which hosts the clinical registry “Diabetes Patient Progress Documentation – DPV.”

Continuous data collection makes it possible to promptly analyze the rates of recent-onset diabetes cases (incidence) and the prevalence of diabetes, as well as trends over time, for North Rhine-Westphalia and Germany.
DIREGT makes an important contribution to diabetes research and healthcare planning—regionally in North Rhine-Westphalia, across Germany, and throughout Europe.

interventions.name: A registry featuring structured data collection and scientific analysis of data on young people with new-onset type 1 and type 2 diabetes in North Rhine-Westphalia and nationwide.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Nationwide: Children aged 0–4 with a physician diagnosed new onset diagnosis of type
1 diabetes who were living in Germany at the time of diagnosis
North Rhine-Westphalia: Children, adolescents, and adults aged 0–34 with a  physician diagnosed new-onset of type 1 or type 2 diabetes who were livivng in North Rhine-Westphalia at the time of diagnosis
Exclusion criteria:
General: No medical diagnosis of Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes at a young age
Nationwide: Place of residence at the time of diagnosis was outside Germany
North Rhine-Westphalia: Place of residence at the time of diagnosis was outside North Rhine-Westphalia
